_readme: Per-city candidate rosters for SpeedShield expansion. NOT fetched by the app. Pipeline: (1) adjudicate each roster against the city's official list (URLs in sources), (2) python3 scripts/build_city_drafts.py --geocode writes drafts/<city>.geocoded.json with sanity-gated coordinates, (3) tester pin-drops a sample / any flagged rows, (4) verified entries are pasted into MANUAL_CAMERAS in update_cameras.py, which is what goes live. Names follow the app convention 'X and Y: City' (speech stops at the colon). direction_deg -1 = omnidirectional; approaches are recorded for the record even though the alert is omnidirectional (Tempe precedent). Compiled 2026-09-02 from search results only -- every official page was network-blocked from the session; see confidence per entry. DIRECTIONAL (2026-09-17, tester decision): where a city publishes the approach a camera enforces, the row carries a "directional" map {"S/B Scottsdale Rd": 180, ...} and the geocoder emits ONE ENTRY PER APPROACH named with the Phoenix prefix convention ("S/B, Scottsdale Rd and McDowell Rd: Scottsdale"; the app strips the prefix for speech and speaks the direction from direction_deg). A null value means the bearing is not yet measured (scripts/measure_road_bearings.py) and the city is not written. Sites enforcing all approaches, and cities that publish no approaches (Chandler, Mesa), stay omnidirectional (-1).

entries.bearing_note: OMNIDIRECTIONAL BY GEOMETRY (2026-09-18, OSM inventory via Woz): Tatum Blvd ENDS at McDonald — every 'North Tatum Boulevard' way lies north of the camera point (S extent -4 m); McDonald's primary carriageways arrive from the WEST at y=-64 m and curve up into Tatum at the camera (way 206896123 spans (-212,-64)->(-5,+4)); McDonald east of Tatum is a minor tertiary leg. 'N/B Tatum' traffic is eastbound McDonald swinging north through a 90-degree bend, which no single direction_deg can carry (a 3-degree axis put the approach 600 m off the corridor at the primary ring -> both tiers suppressed). Both through movements are enforced, so -1 costs only the minor eastern leg. Earlier measurements: S/B 183.0 (near 191 / far 184, dev 45 m); N/B provisional 3 — RETIRED.

albuquerque.status: CANDIDATE 2026-09-18 (research only, nothing staged). City of Albuquerque Automated Speed Enforcement: FIXED pole cameras, mid-block or near an intersection, ONE DIRECTION OF TRAVEL each (the city states it), go-live dates published per camera; $100 civil fine; 38 active per the city's page as summarised 2026-09 (34 in June + 2 in July + 2 on 2026-07-29 + 2 on 2026-09-04). Ordinance 21-69 (signed 2021-10-15) also allows MOBILE units -- none are listed with locations, so mobile is out of scope like Phoenix's. The 32 rows below (36 approaches) are from web-search SUMMARIES of the official page, not a verbatim read: the Claude for Chrome capture in SpeedShield docs/EXPANSION_RESEARCH_ABQ_LA_2026-09.md is the adjudication step. Geocoding: OSM street names in Albuquerque carry a quadrant suffix ('Gibson Boulevard Southeast') -- check osm_street_name matching on the first Woz run; mid-block rows use the new 'A between B and C' query form (midpoint of the two intersections); every approach heading must be measured (measure_road_bearings.py) before the city is written. Legal: no NM ban activity; 2026 SB 91 would let the city keep 100% of fines.
sources: https://www.cabq.gov/automated-speed-enforcement (official list: every camera with direction of travel and go-live date; the page to capture VERBATIM with Claude for Chrome)

not_in_scope.san_bernardino_city: NONE (2026-09-18): no automated speed enforcement (not an AB 645 pilot city; only Caltrans' AB 289 work-zone pilot could touch the area and it is state-run, unpublished); the red-light camera program was ended by a 5-0 council vote in March 2011 and the cameras removed. 2026 'safety camera' news is Flock/surveillance cameras, not enforcement
